meta.notes_for_ui: Menstrual phase (day 3). Stability-first nutrition to support energy, focus, and training performance. Mild cravings expected.

baseline_principles.label: Regular intake
baseline_principles.why: Regular meals tend to stabilise blood sugar and cortisol, supporting hormonal signalling and recovery.
how_to_apply: Keep meals consistent day to day
Avoid long gaps that leave you depleted

baseline_principles.label: Protein at each meal
baseline_principles.why: Protein supports muscle repair, satiety, and cognitive clarity during training weeks.
how_to_apply: Use mixed plant and animal sources as preferred

baseline_principles.label: Carbs matched to training
baseline_principles.why: Carbohydrates reduce stress load and usually improve performance tolerance, especially in women.
how_to_apply: Slightly more carb support on training mornings
Moderate, steady carbs on rest days

baseline_principles.label: Avoid very low fat intake
baseline_principles.why: Dietary fat supports estrogen and progesterone production and overall hormonal stability.
how_to_apply: Avoid unintentionally cutting fats too low

physiology_focus.cycle_context: Early menstrual phase with recovery in progress and energy rebuilding.
physiology_focus.implication: Energy availability and stress regulation matter more than optimisation right now.
physiology_focus.this_week_priority: Consistency and gentle fuel support to restore energy and focus.

protein_g_per_kg_per_day.note: Reference band, not a target. Spread intake across meals.

carb_orientation.training_days: Moderate to slightly higher carb support tends to help energy and performance.
carb_orientation.rest_days: Moderate, steady carb intake usually supports recovery without heaviness.
carb_orientation.note: Earlier-day carbs often support mood and sleep.

fat_floor.guidance: Avoid very low fat intake across the day.
fat_floor.note: Daily inclusion supports hormonal function and satiety.

meal_timing.note: Your current 3-meal rhythm fits well here.

daily_orientation.title: Morning training support
daily_orientation.aim: Support energy and performance without heaviness.

trigger.label: mild_cravings
trigger.explanation: Cravings usually reflect higher energy demand during cycle transition, not lack of discipline.

adjustments.label: Earlier carb support
adjustments.why: Slightly higher carbs earlier can reduce evening cravings and support sleep.
how: Shift some carbs to earlier meals
Pair carbs with protein for stability

adjustments.label: Meal completeness
adjustments.why: Incomplete meals often drive later hunger and cravings.

if_then_rules.if: Cravings show up late in the day
if_then_rules.then: Consider whether earlier meals were too light or carb-restricted

guardrails.label: No aggressive restriction
guardrails.reason: Low energy availability can worsen fatigue and impair training recovery.

guardrails.label: No fasting strategies
guardrails.reason: Regular intake better supports hormones and cognitive clarity this week.

closing_note: This week favors steadiness over optimisation. Consistent meals with enough protein, carbs, and fats tend to restore energy and support performance without adding stress.
